subject: Standby sizing request: Meridian Robotics - late-stage commitment
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 23 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Standby sizing request: Meridian Robotics - late-stage commitment

Team —

Meridian (cc'd later) just moved to legal and procurement; deal team expects a signature window within 10 business days. Engineering expects production traffic pattern that will need an initial pool of ~40 A100-equivalent cards for the first 3 months of the rollout (see attached spreadsheet for per-region footprint). Can we do a short availability scan and a "soft standby" authorization? Key asks:

- Confirm current A100-equivalent spare capacity in us-west/us-east for 90-day blocks.
- Identify any immediate opportunities to repack lower-priority pools to free up ~12-15 cards.
- If we can’t meet 40, what's the earliest ramp plan (week-by-week) and whether a regional split (30 us-west / 10 us-east) is feasible.

I’m asking for a capacity flag in HubSpot and a one-paragraph summary I can share with Meridian procurement. Attaching meridian_capacity_request_v2.xlsx with their requested schedule.

If we can grant a soft hold (not contractual, just an ops reservation) that would materially reduce procurement friction on their side — they’ve indicated a hard close timeline.

Thanks — Sean

--
Sean Gallagher
Account Executive, Enterprise
Redwood Inference
sean_gallagher@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0123

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 23 Aug 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Standby sizing request: Meridian Robotics - late-stage commitment

Sean / team —

Quick scan of current inventory and scheduled maintenance: we do not have 40 A100s idle right now. Snapshot:

- us-west: 18 spare A100-equivalents available for immediate allocation.
- us-east: 9 spare.
- Additional ~8 cards become free on 2026-09-01 as a short-term lease rolls off.

We can free another 6-10 cards by compressing lower-priority batch jobs and shifting some dedicated test pools to preemptible mode, but that will need a formal ops change window and will add churn for internal teams. Estimated realistic immediate deliverable: 33 cards (18+9+6) with a staged ramp to 41 by week 2 of Sept if we trigger the lease-cycle reassign and the 09-01 rolloff goes as scheduled.

Risks / notes:
- If Meridian needs strict single-region placement (all 40 in us-west), that’s tougher — we’d only be able to place ~28 in us-west without impacting committed dedicated customers.
- A "soft standby" is fine from ops side as an internal flag, but we’ll need sign-off from Capacity Planning (Laura) for any >30-day reservation that affects financial forecasts.

I’ve attached a short capacity worksheet and included tentative reassign windows. Let me know if you want me to propose a specific 2-week ops change schedule to free additional cards.

Ben

Attachments: meridian_capacity_request_v2.xlsx (referenced), internal_capacity_scan_aug23.csv (stub)

--
Ben Carter
Head of Capacity Planning
Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: John Sullivan <john.sullivan@meridian.ai>, procurement@meridian.ai
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 23 Aug 2026 14:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Standby sizing request: Meridian Robotics - late-stage commitment

John / Meridian team —

Thanks for the quick momentum here. To be transparent on ops: we can commit to a soft standby equivalent to 33 A100s immediately (regionally split per Ben’s note). We can work toward 41 by early September if your timeline can accommodate a small staged ramp.

Proposed next steps to keep the cadence moving:

1) I’ll share a one-paragraph internal summary for your procurement that confirms a soft standby (non-binding) and the tentative ramp dates.
2) John — can you confirm whether Meridian can accept a two-region split (primary us-west + us-east overflow) for the initial weeks? That will speed the hold.
3) We’ll provision a draft SLA and the ops change schedule for your legal review (attached is a draft SLA for initial review).

If you prefer all-in single-region placement as a condition for signature, call that out and we’ll escalate capacity consequences (and a longer ramp).

Best — Vanessa

--
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Sales Manager, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai

From: John Sullivan <john.sullivan@meridian.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 24 Aug 2026 15:48:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Standby sizing request: Meridian Robotics - late-stage commitment

Vanessa / team —

Appreciate the transparency. Meridian can accept a two-region split for the initial 2–3 weeks as long as the SLA covers regional failover and we get the full 40 cards by Sept 7 at the latest. Procurement is lining up signatures and would like the proposed SLA and a soft hold confirmation to appear on our PO paperwork as a contingency note.

Please send the SLA draft and a short ops ramp schedule (week-by-week) and we’ll circulate with legal. If you can flag the soft standby in HubSpot that helps our procurement reference it internally.

We’re ready to proceed pending the SLA and the hold. Thanks — John

--
John Sullivan
Head of ML Infrastructure
Meridian Robotics
john.sullivan@meridian.ai
